bug_semantics: Parcel's development server unconditionally attached `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (plus permissive methods and headers) to static-file responses. While a developer had the server running, JavaScript on a malicious website visited by that developer could fetch predictable localhost URLs, read the HTML and emitted script responses cross-origin, and exfiltrate source code. The released 2.16.4 mitigation is opt-in: `--no-cors` propagates `cors: false` and suppresses those response headers so the browser's same-origin policy blocks the read; the permissive behavior remains the default.
flaw_origin: PR #713 implemented the requested CORS feature from issue #570 by wiring a new `enableCors` callback into `serve-static` and setting the allowed origin to `*`. The reconstructable one-commit PR member `d9b20c020c73f63ad7e4375e104277f162c098a5` is the smallest BIC; GitHub squash-landed its identical patch as `1c761fd5683d9bf195ee5eb6fd04bd494ecb6162`. Parcel 2 later carried the same mechanism into `packages/reporters/dev-server/src/Server.js` (the vulnerable header there traces to `81117b45fd5e1f017a4be528a3652bdd089b7c15`), but that later port is not the first origin.

The vulnerability-first trace starts with the advisory's XHR source-disclosure claim and the PoC's concrete browser-to-localhost attack. The decisive flawed mechanism is not generic dev-server exposure but Parcel's explicit wildcard CORS response, which lets attacker-origin JavaScript read responses. Line history leads to squash `1c761fd5683d9bf195ee5eb6fd04bd494ecb6162`; the surviving PR patch reconstructs its sole original member `d9b20c020c73f63ad7e4375e104277f162c098a5`, and stable patch IDs prove the member and landed squash apply the same `src/Server.js` change. The member's immediate parent lacks every vulnerable CORS line, so the member is the smallest BIC rather than the later Parcel 2 port. Tag trees establish a clean pre-BIC release at 1.5.1 and reveal that 1.6.0 already contains the flaw despite the advisory starting at 1.6.1. At the upper boundary, direct parent `73f691d67d22482440babb2d1846b7da2160f7cc` is version 2.16.3, while `9e2f6f1377123cff3b82f6dde4e20336efc846a1` adds the opt-in suppression and is contained in v2.16.4; the stronger `4bc56e3242a85491c7edf589966e9b44c6330c49` proposal never landed. Finally, the exact decomposed BIC commit object has only human author/committer identities and no AI marker. Under BIC-only attribution, the closed verdict is therefore NOT_AI.
